clue.text: Complain about new performer as Lady Bountiful?

indicators.note: one word goes about the other, wrapping round it on both sides

blocks.note: to beef is slang for to grumble
N is the standard abbreviation for new
a female performer on stage

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a newcomer on stage who plays the generous lady of the manor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complain' looks like the start of a sentence, but it is slang that holds the abbreviation. Lady Bountiful is a charitable character in Farquhar's play The Beaux' Stratagem.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Bountiful has become a byword for a woman who hands out charity, which is exactly what a female patron or donor does.

clue.text: Hounds or what they may seek

blocks.note: first meaning: pesters persistently, as a verb
second meaning: the burrowing animals that hunting dogs are sent after

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hounds' looks like a plural noun for dogs, but it is the verb; the second half reads the dogs literally and names their quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to nag them relentlessly, and badgers are also the animals dachshunds were bred to dig out.

clue.text: Service upset about female entry? By no means!

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns the letters upside down so they run bottom to top
the turned letters are placed around the other piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: RN is the Royal Navy, the senior armed service
Eve, the first female to enter the world in Genesis

explanation.surface: A question about whether women may join the armed services, answered with a firm refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue: everything before it is wordplay, and the exclamation is the definition. Eve is the first woman in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Never is an emphatic refusal meaning not at any time, the same flat denial as the exclamation in the clue.

clue.text: Agitator appeared to inspire Ibsen character

blocks.note: to fire someone up is to inspire them
Brand is the title character of Ibsen's verse play

explanation.surface: A rabble-rouser turned up to stir one of Ibsen's heroes into action.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebrand is a person who stirs up trouble or passion in others, an agitator in politics or society.

clue.text: Chastened husband in police custody

indicators.note: one piece is placed in, held within, the other

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A husband taken into police custody is suitably humbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'custody' completes the picture of the husband held by the CID; chid is the old past tense of chide.
explanation.definitionFit: Chid is an archaic past tense of chide, meaning scolded or rebuked, which is what chastened means as a verb.

clue.text: Noted architect beheaded, having confessed

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is cut away

blocks.note: Sir Christopher Wren, architect of St Paul's Cathedral
to own up, or own, is to confess

explanation.surface: A famous architect is executed after admitting his guilt.
explanation.walkthrough: Wren is the architect crosswords reach for first; 'having confessed' means having admitted to, as in owning up.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted and renowned are synonyms for famous, well known and widely celebrated.

clue.text: Women not wanted on this board

definitions.text: Women not wanted on this board

blocks.clueFragment: Women not wanted on this board
blocks.note: surface reading: a committee or company board that excludes women
setter's reading: a flat plank fixed to a wall, where unmarried women were said to be left, unwanted

explanation.walkthrough: The old idiom 'left on the shelf' describes a woman thought past marrying age; a shelf is literally a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf is a horizontal board, and the idiom for women nobody wanted to marry places them upon one.

clue.text: Zone in which! soldiers join supreme commander in exercises

indicators.note: the joined pieces are placed in the abbreviation for exercises

blocks.note: PT is physical training, school exercises
RE is the Royal Engineers
C-in-C, commander-in-chief

explanation.surface: An area where troops and their commander-in-chief come together on manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark after 'which' is a printing blemish on the page. C-in-C is the standard military shorthand for commander-in-chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A precinct is a defined district or enclosed area, such as a shopping or police precinct, so a zone.

clue.text: Sleeping accommodation available for small charge

definitions.text: Sleeping accommodation available for small charge

blocks.clueFragment: Sleeping accommodation available for small charge
blocks.note: surface reading: a cheap bed for the night at a low price
setter's reading: a charge is a person in one's care, and a small one is a baby

explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' reads as a fee, but it means a dependant; the bed is for an infant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradle is a small rocking bed made for a baby, the little one in a parent's care.

clue.text: Turning aside from amusement

blocks.note: first meaning: a rerouting away from the usual course
second meaning: a pastime or entertainment

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, turning away from fun, but splits into two meanings around 'from'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is both a deflection from a path, like a traffic detour, and a recreation that distracts the mind.

clue.text: Dread loss of opener to slip

indicators.note: losing the opener means the word's first letter is dropped

blocks.note: dread is great fear

explanation.surface: A batsman fears losing his opening partner to a catch in the slips.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture misleads: opener and slip are not cricket here. A slip is a fielding position near the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, and an error is a mistake, so the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: Brought back Egyptian costume

indicators.note: sent back means the letters run right to left

blocks.note: borne is the past participle of bear, to bring or carry
E is the abbreviation for Egyptian

explanation.surface: Someone has fetched home an outfit from Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: BORNE reversed gives ENROB, then E: ENROBE. 'costume' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To costume someone is to dress them, and to enrobe is to clothe in a robe or garment.

clue.text: Insincere, like Janus, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: deceitful, saying different things to different people
second meaning: literally having two faces, as the Roman god of doorways is shown

explanation.walkthrough: Janus, Roman god of beginnings, is depicted with two faces looking opposite ways; 'perhaps' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a hypocrite and the literal description of the double-headed Roman god coincide in one compound.

clue.text: Cue for reappearance to sing a number

indicators.note: a reappearance shows the word again in a new form, so its letters are reset

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A performer gets the prompt to come back on stage and sing a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a song, but it is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal is a sign or prompt to act, which is what a cue is for an actor or performer.

clue.text: State with very little illumination

blocks.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia, a US state
slight means small or scanty

explanation.surface: Somewhere is so poorly lit that it barely has any light at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with very little illumination' reads as one phrase, but 'illumination' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaslight is the lighting produced by burning coal gas in lamps, the standard street illumination of Victorian times.

clue.text: Leopard seen by lair in grass

blocks.note: a den is a wild animal's lair
the ounce is the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A big cat is spotted beside its den out in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is the British slang verb meaning to inform on someone to the police, not the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass on someone is to inform against them, and denouncing is publicly accusing or reporting a person.

clue.text: Telling too many tales to obtain superior position

blocks.note: first meaning: fibbing excessively, read as two words
second meaning: lying on top of something else

explanation.walkthrough: Split as OVERLY LYING, it is lying too much; as one word it describes resting on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlie means to lie over or upon, so overlying is occupying the upper place; read apart it is excessive fibbing.

clue.text: Puffed-up learner defiant when corrected

blocks.note: L is the learner driver's plate
taken as written

explanation.surface: An arrogant, rebellious pupil is put in his place.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something swollen with air, or figuratively a person full of self-importance.

clue.text: Dweller in desert is nomadic

indicators.note: nomads wander, so these letters roam into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who lives in the desert is a wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is ironic: a resident stays put, the opposite of nomadic.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is a person who lives in a particular place, an inhabitant or occupant.

clue.text: Chatter briskly - it amuses the baby

blocks.note: first meaning: talk rapidly
second meaning: a toy that makes a noise when shaken

explanation.walkthrough: The two parts look like cause and effect, a parent talking to a baby, but each defines the word separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle on is to talk quickly and at length, and a rattle is a noisy toy given to infants.

clue.text: The game may be up for him

definitions.text: The game may be up for him

blocks.clueFragment: The game may be up for him
blocks.note: surface reading: someone whose scheme has been found out
setter's reading: game birds that this man drives up into the air for the guns

explanation.walkthrough: 'The game is up' means you are caught; here game is birds, flushed up at a shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: At a pheasant or grouse shoot, workers walk through cover striking it to drive the birds into flight.

clue.text: Withdraw to sanctuary

blocks.note: first meaning: pull back, as a verb
second meaning: a quiet refuge, as a noun

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one instruction, go to a safe place, but the verb and the noun are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreat is both the act of pulling back from danger and a secluded place of refuge or rest.

clue.text: Instrument relating to reform

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A legal or political device concerned with reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests a legal document, but it is the musical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangle is a percussion instrument, a steel bar bent into three sides and struck with a beater.

clue.text: Tender found by railwaymen on points

blocks.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen
S and E are two compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: A railway tender is discovered by the workers at the points.
explanation.walkthrough: A tender is a coal wagon behind a locomotive and points are rail switches, but here tender is a carer and points are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse is someone who tends the sick, so a tender in the sense of one who looks after people.

clue.text: Plastic factory closing about one

indicators.note: closing about means shutting around, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: a plant is an industrial works

explanation.surface: A plastics factory is shutting down around one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' looks like the material the factory makes, but it is an adjective meaning mouldable.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic in its older sense means easily shaped or moulded, and pliant means flexible or yielding.

clue.text: Conscious respect surrounding rising artist

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom upwards

explanation.definitionFit: Conscious and aware are synonyms meaning having knowledge or perception of something.

clue.text: Brownie leader bolted cereal

blocks.note: the start of the word Brownie

explanation.definitionFit: Bran is the husk of cereal grain, eaten as a breakfast cereal, so it fits the general word.
